newsitem.title: USA: Retired U.S. admiral accused of fraternization.
newsitem.headline: Retired U.S. admiral accused of fraternization.

text.p: Retired Pacific commander Adm. Richard Macke improperly fraternised with a junior officer, misusing a Navy plane and military telephones in their relationship, according to a report released on Tuesday.
Macke and the woman both denied they had a sexual relationship but exercised their right not to talk to Navy investigators, the Navy inspector general report said.
"We conclude that Adm. Macke and (the woman) violated the Navy policy prohibiting fraternisation by engaging in an unduly familiar relationship," the report said.
The Navy and other U.S. military services prohibit close personal friendships between officers and lower-ranking people as "prejudicial to good order and discipline."
It also concluded that Macke misused a Navy plane by holding it and its crew in San Diego for three days at a cost of $3,600 while he took a trip with the woman and her mother.
It said military telephones were used for more than 850 long distance telephone calls between them at a cost of $2,786, only part of which was reimbursed.
Macke was commander of U.S. forces in the Pacific with headquarters in Hawaii. The woman was on the West Coast but most information about her was blacked out of the report.
Defence Secretary William Perry forced Macke to retire last April after he told reporters that three Marines accused of raping a 12-year-old girl in Okinawa should have hired a prostitute instead.
Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon said the Navy sent Macke and the woman punitive letters and Macke retired at a grade that reduced his pension.
"I think this issue is closed," Bacon said.

The report said Macke told Navy investigators in a written statement that the woman and her mother were family friends and that he had no influence over her career. "There has been no fraternisation," it quoted his statement as saying.
It said the woman also made a statement that "although she and Admiral Macke have a personal relationship, it was never physical, sexual or romantic."
The report said hotel records of the three-day trip they took showed the woman and her mother stayed in one room and Macke in another.
